profile_notes: Street photography suits a body that disappears into the scene and responds instantly to a fleeting moment. Handling is weighted highest (3): discretion, quick physical controls, and a rangefinder-style / walk-around feel are the genre's signature, and reviewers consistently frame 'responsive controls' and a small, low-profile body as what lets subjects behave naturally. autofocus_body (2) matches the value placed on fast, reliable eye/subject-detect for candid movement, but is held below handling because a large share of street work is done with zone/snap/pre-focus, so AF is important without being defining. sensor_performance (1) and image_quality (1) carry low-light/high-ISO (night street) and rendering, kept modest because the genre prizes the moment over ultimate IQ. evf_lcd (1) supports quick composition and waist-level/tilt candid framing. GATE = require:[] BY DESIGN and by population reality: the compactness that matters to street lives in the weight_g / dimensions_mm SPECS, and neither is in the engine's predicate vocab (specs.py KNOWN_PREDICATES = resolution_mp, card_slots, sensor_format, iso_native, ibis_stops); weight_g is also present on only ~12/47 bodies, so any hard size ceiling would exclude most of the corpus as backfill rather than rank it. Discretion is therefore expressed through the handling weight and the lexicon, not a gate. gear_class excludes only 'novelty' (junk floor). NOT weighted: af_performance and color_rendition are in the allowed body list but appear on ZERO body cards in the current corpus, so weighting them would be inert (and would fail C1 axis validation); quiet/silent-shutter has no dedicated axis and is only partly captured by handling/build.
